item.title: Apple Unveils MacBook Neo, Priced at USD 599, Targeting Budget PC Market
item.description: Apple has unveiled the MacBook Neo, a new lower-priced laptop starting at USD 599, aiming to broaden its reach in the price-sensitive personal computer market. This launch comes as rival companies face tighter supplies of memory chips.

item.title: Google Overhauls Android App Store Policies, Fortnite Returns
item.description: Google announced major changes to its Android app store, expanding billing options, and reducing developer fees. This move resolved a long-running dispute with Epic Games and led to Fortnite's return to the Google Play Store in the U.S. in December, following the lawsuit settlement. Google also announced policy changes that would enable Fortnite's worldwide return.

item.title: Xiaomi Unveils Vision GT Electric Supercar Concept
item.description: Xiaomi has unveiled a Vision Gran Turismo concept supercar at MWC 2026 in Barcelona, becoming the first Chinese automaker to join the iconic racing game’s concept car program in its 28-year history. This marks a significant step for the tech company in the high-performance automotive sector.

item.title: Higher Education in the Spotlight of the AI Surge
item.description: As Generative AI floods university campuses, a pressing question emerges: Are academic institutions genuinely evolving, or are they simply scrambling to protect an outdated system?

item.title: Amazon AWS Launches AI Platform for Healthcare Administration
item.description: Amazon's cloud unit, AWS, has launched an artificial intelligence-enabled platform designed to improve patient access to care and reduce administrative tasks for healthcare providers. The new platform, Amazon Connect Health, aims to streamline operations within the healthcare sector.

item.title: X Investigates Grok Chatbot Over Offensive Posts
item.description: Social media platform X is investigating "racist and offensive" posts generated by xAI's chatbot Grok. Sky News reported the investigation.

item.title: China Sees OpenClaw AI Rush Amidst Privacy Debates
item.description: Consumers across southern China are rapidly adopting OpenClaw, an open-source artificial intelligence agent, for diverse tasks despite intensifying privacy concerns surrounding the technology. The widespread enthusiasm for OpenClaw has prompted a rush by Chinese tech companies to capitalise on its popularity.

item.title: Australians Turn to VPNs Amidst New Online Age Restrictions
item.description: Australians are increasingly downloading virtual private networks, known as VPNs, as the country rolled out sweeping online age restrictions. These measures have led one of the world's largest pornography distributors to block users from its platforms. item.title: Nexperia China Starts Chip Production Amid Independence Dispute
item.description: Nexperia China has commenced producing its own chips, marking a significant step towards independence from its Dutch parent. The Chinese subsidiary is utilising 12-inch wafers, a size that Nexperia’s European facilities cannot manufacture. item.title: Microsoft Integrates Anthropic AI into Copilot for Enterprise Agents
item.description: Microsoft is integrating artificial intelligence technology from Anthropic into its Copilot service to meet demand for autonomous agents. The company on Monday unveiled Copilot Cowork, a tool based on Anthropic’s viral Claude Cowork offering, which has captivated Silicon Valley with its ability to handle complex tasks.
